steps.title: A table of contents and six images
steps.body: A FIP is a table of contents (one UUID, offset and size per image) followed by the images. BL2 asks for each image by UUID, so the order does not matter. The bar is drawn to scale; the table below gives the exact numbers from a real build.

steps.title: OP-TEE header: how to start OP-TEE
steps.body: A 44-byte header (`--tos-fw`, passed as `BL32=`). BL2 reads it to learn OP-TEE's entry point and the sizes of the other two OP-TEE files.

steps.title: OP-TEE pager: the part that stays in on-chip RAM
steps.body: `tee-pager_v2.bin`, 74,648 bytes (`--tos-fw-extra1`). It holds the resident core, including the SCMI server, and runs from the on-chip SRAM.

steps.title: OP-TEE pageable: the rest, loaded on demand
steps.body: `tee-pageable_v2.bin`, 364,544 bytes (`--tos-fw-extra2`). OP-TEE's pager copies pages of it into the on-chip RAM as they are needed. The pager is on by default for this chip, which is why OP-TEE is three images here and two on the 64-bit board.

steps.title: U-Boot: the biggest part
steps.body: `u-boot-nodtb.bin` (`--nt-fw`, `BL33=`), 1,098,696 bytes, loaded by BL2 to `0xC0100000` in normal-world DDR. "Non-trusted firmware" is TF-A's name for the normal-world bootloader.

steps.title: fw-config: BL2's load plan
steps.body: A tiny device tree (`--fw-config`) built from `fdts/` that says where each image goes and how the TZC-400 memory firewall is divided: the top 32 MiB of DDR secure for OP-TEE, the rest non-secure.

steps.title: U-Boot's own device tree
steps.body: `u-boot.dtb` (`--hw-config`, `BL33_CFG=`), loaded to `0xC0500000`. It is the tree U-Boot itself uses: it names the console, the SD controller and the environment partition.

steps.title: What is not in here
steps.body: No BL31 and no DDR firmware, because this 32-bit chip needs neither; and BL2 itself is not in the FIP, because the Boot ROM already loaded it from `fsbl1`. The whole FIP is about 1.6 MB in a 4 MiB partition.
